title: Two Mirrors, Many Images
description: Umbra clones himself in a hall of mirrors! To find the real one, learn how two mirrors at an angle create many images.

content.value: Place an object between two mirrors set at an angle and you see several images. The smaller the angle between the mirrors, the MORE images appear — because the light reflects back and forth many times.
For two plane mirrors at an angle, the number of images is found with a neat formula: (360 ÷ angle) − 1.

Number of images = (360 / angle) − 1

Angle 90°  →  360/90 − 1 = 3 images
Angle 60°  →  360/60 − 1 = 5 images
Angle 45°  →  360/45 − 1 = 7 images
Angle 0° (parallel) → infinite images!
When two mirrors face each other parallel (like in a barber's shop), you see an endless tunnel of images — the light bounces back and forth almost forever, each reflection a little dimmer.
Smaller angle = more images. This is exactly the trick a kaleidoscope uses to make beautiful repeating patterns.
Key Takeaway: Two mirrors at an angle form multiple images. The number is (360 ÷ angle) − 1, and parallel mirrors give infinite images.

quiz.question: Two plane mirrors are set at 60°. How many images of an object form between them?
As the angle between two mirrors gets SMALLER, the number of images…
quiz.explain: A smaller angle means more reflections, so more images form. At 0° (parallel) the images become infinite.

quiz.question: Two mirrors placed parallel and facing each other produce…
quiz.explain: Parallel facing mirrors reflect light back and forth endlessly, creating a tunnel of many images, each dimmer than the last.
